edits.text: 1. POSITION; DUTIES; REPORTING. The Executive shall serve as Chief Operating Officer and shall have duties, authority, and responsibilities commensurate with that position and as reasonably assigned from time to time by the Chief Executive Officer or the Board of Directors. The Executive shall report to the Chief Executive Officer. The Company shall not materially diminish the Executive’s title, duties, authority, or reporting relationship except in connection with a bona fide Company-wide restructuring or as otherwise agreed in writing by the Executive.
edits.name: Position; Duties; Reporting

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION; BENEFITS; EXPENSES. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary as set forth in Schedule A, less applicable withholdings, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the Company’s annual bonus, equity incentive, retirement, health, welfare, and other generally applicable benefit plans and programs, subject in each case to the terms of those plans and programs as in effect from time to time. The Company shall reimburse the Executive for reasonable and documented business expenses incurred in the performance of the Executive’s duties, subject to the Company’s expense reimbursement policies as in effect from time to time.
edits.name: Compensation; Benefits; Expenses

edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, then, subject to the Executive’s execution and non-revocation of a general release of claims in favor of the Company in a form reasonably acceptable to the Company and the Executive’s continued compliance with all surviving restrictive covenant and confidentiality obligations, the Executive shall receive the severance benefits set forth in Schedule A. Cash severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices beginning on the first regular payroll date after the release becomes effective and irrevocable; provided that any installments that otherwise would have been paid before such date shall be paid with the first installment. Any severance remains subject to applicable tax withholding and Section 409A compliance procedures.
edits.name: Severance

edits.text: 4. RESTRICTIVE COVENANT. During employment and for twelve months following the Executive’s departure, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in or provide services to a Competing Business in a Restricted Capacity within the Restricted Territory; provided that this Section shall apply only to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law and shall not prohibit passive ownership of less than two percent of the outstanding securities of a publicly traded company. For purposes of this Section: (a) “Competing Business” means a business that offers products or services competitive with products or services offered by the Company and as to which the Executive had material involvement or access to Confidential Information during the final twelve months of employment; (b) “Restricted Capacity” means a role or function that is the same as or substantially similar to services the Executive performed for the Company or in which the Executive would be reasonably expected to use or disclose Confidential Information; and (c) “Restricted Territory” means any market or geographic area in which the Executive had material involvement or about which the Executive received Confidential Information during the final twelve months of employment. If any restriction is found overbroad, it shall be modified and enforced to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.
edits.name: Restrictive Covenant

edits.text: 5. DEFINITIONS. “Cause” means: (a) the Executive’s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or any crime involving fraud, dishonesty, or moral turpitude; (b) willful misconduct or gross negligence in the performance of the Executive’s duties that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company; (c) material breach of this Agreement or any material written Company policy applicable to senior executives; (d) fraud, embezzlement, or misappropriation involving the Company; or (e) willful failure to perform the Executive’s material duties after written notice and, if reasonably curable, a period of thirty days to cure. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent: (i) a material diminution in base salary, other than an across-the-board reduction applicable to similarly situated senior executives; (ii) a material diminution in title, duties, authority, or reporting relationship; (iii) relocation of the Executive’s principal place of employment by more than fifty miles; or (iv) the Company’s material breach of this Agreement; provided that the Executive gives written notice within ninety days after the event constituting Good Reason, the Company has thirty days to cure, and the Executive resigns within thirty days after the cure period expires if the condition has not been cured.
edits.name: Definitions

edits.text: 6. INDEMNIFICATION; D&O INSURANCE. The Company shall indemnify the Executive to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Company’s organizational documents for acts or omissions occurring within the scope of the Executive’s service to the Company. During employment and for so long thereafter as claims may be brought against the Executive arising from such service, the Company shall maintain directors’ and officers’ liability insurance coverage for the Executive on terms no less favorable than those provided to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the terms of the applicable policy.
edits.name: Indemnification; D&O Insurance

edits.text:
SCHEDULE A

Base Salary: $425,000 per year.

Target Annual Bonus: 50% of annual base salary, subject to achievement of applicable Company and individual performance objectives and the terms of the Company’s annual bonus plan. Except as otherwise provided in this Agreement or an applicable plan document, the Executive must remain employed through the applicable payment date to receive an annual bonus.

Equity: The Executive will be eligible for equity awards under the Company’s equity incentive plan, as determined by the Board or Compensation Committee in its discretion and subject to the applicable plan and award agreements.

Severance Amount: Upon a qualifying termination by the Company without Cause or resignation by the Executive for Good Reason, the Executive shall receive: (a) twelve months of continued base salary; (b) any earned but unpaid annual bonus for a completed prior year, payable when bonuses are generally paid to senior executives; and (c) subject to the Executive’s timely election of COBRA continuation coverage and continued eligibility, Company-paid or reimbursed COBRA premiums for up to twelve months, ending earlier if the Executive becomes eligible for comparable coverage from another employer.
edits.name: Schedule A
